takeaways.label: Strong quarter, guidance intact
takeaways.text: Consolidated revenue grew 34% YoY, with management reaffirming 20% revenue growth and profitability outpacing revenue for FY27.

takeaways.label: Jammu crosses breakeven
takeaways.text: The Jammu facility posted its first positive EBITDA of ₹1 crore to ₹1.5 crore in Q1, with revenue of ~₹107 crore and healthy season still ahead from Q2.

takeaways.label: Volume is the engine
takeaways.text: Of the 34% revenue growth, ~20–22% was volume growth at manufacturing capability level, with the remainder from favorable product/sales mix and pricing.

takeaways.label: Margin story is a Jammu story
takeaways.text: Non-Jammu margin runs at ~20% while Jammu sits at 1–1.5%, pulling consolidated margin to ~16%; management sees Jammu reaching 17–18% margin, which would lift the consolidated profile.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether Jammu's ramp continues into the healthy season, whether gross margin holds near 35.5%, and whether management signals any upgrade to the 20%-plus growth guidance.

points.label: Revenue trajectory
points.text: Jammu posted Q1 revenue of ~₹107 crore versus ~₹90 crore in Q4 FY26, with management stating the ramp-up is pacing as expected. Q1 typically carries seasonal impact, with the healthy season starting from Q2 onwards.

points.label: Profitability inflection
points.text: Jammu achieved positive EBITDA of ₹1 crore to ₹1.5 crore this quarter, crossing the breakeven line for the first time.

points.label: Optimum scale
points.text: Jammu plant optimum revenue is anticipated at ₹1,400 crore at utilization of 65% to 70%, with asset turns expected north of 3x at optimum level.

points.label: Margin convergence
points.text: Once Jammu crosses breakeven, its margin profile will move in line with the base business; management expects Jammu to reach 17% to 18% margin, which from a base of 16% should upgrade the consolidated margin by 2% to 3% when Jammu starts giving contributing margin.

points.label: Revenue milestone
points.text: Jammu can cross the ₹1,000 crore revenue mark once onboarding of countries, products, and customers completes; by end of this financial year, the company may have product approvals from different markets for Jammu.

quotes.text: Lokesh Bhasin: "Jammu, Jammu ramp-up is pacing up the way we expected. So, we should also consider that normally quarter one, there is a seasonal impact of the entire year. And from, see, from Q2 onwards the normal healthy season start picking up."

points.label: CDMO growth
points.text: 32% YoY growth driven by expanding product portfolio, addition of new customers, and deeper engagement with existing customers resulting in higher wallet share.

points.label: Branded generic growth
points.text: 39% YoY growth supported by continued traction across key markets; management sees branded generic as a significant opportunity over the medium and long term to diversify revenue base and strengthen presence across key markets.

points.label: No conflict between segments
points.text: From a plant perspective, branded generic business is treated as a normal CDMO customer, with no additional or special treatment.

points.label: Sharon performance
points.text: Sharon had a seasonal impact on performance this quarter; full-year expectation is continued growth in line with organic business expectations, in the early teens.

quotes.text: Lokesh Bhasin: "So, from a plant perspective, from a manufacturing capability business, this our branded generic business is just considered as a normal CDMO customer by our plant. So, from that particular viewpoint, there is no, I would say, additional treatment or any special treatment for our branded generic business."

points.label: Gross margin dip
points.text: YoY dip of 1% to 1.5% attributed to overall business mix changes, described as normal course of business. Full-year gross margin expected to maintain around 35.5% plus/minus 2%.

points.label: Other expenses
points.text: Percentage basis slightly reduced YoY; absolute increase commensurate with operations growth. Slight increase in logistics costs due to conflict, duly factored in and not material.

points.label: Margin guidance
points.text: Management maintained margin guidance at 15% to 16% plus-minus 2%; once Jammu starts giving good EBITDA margin, overall margin at 15% to 16% level should expand.

points.label: Pricing environment
points.text: This quarter prices trended toward the increase side; management able to pass through pricing to customers at a certain level.

quotes.text: Vinay Lohariwala: "Assuming 20% is very high expectation. I think it 17%, 18% is the fair number."

points.label: Volume growth
points.text: 20% to 22% volume growth at overall manufacturing capability level came from existing capabilities contributing to growth, optimization of resources, and operating leverage benefits.

points.label: Volume guidance
points.text: Management maintained volume growth guidance at north of 20% on volume basis, and is very confident of 20% plus volume growth in the coming period.

points.label: Strategic priorities
points.text: Improving capacity utilization, expanding complex dosage form capabilities, strengthening R&D platforms, deepening customer relationships, and expanding branded generic presence.

points.label: Future expansion
points.text: Likely in tranches of ₹200 crore to ₹250 crore rather than large single investments; will expand in saturated categories (general Baddi portfolio, core Baddi portfolio) and open new dosage forms or therapeutic categories where currently not present.

points.label: Baddi plot
points.text: New plot bought last year; plan remains on same line, still being firmed up; will come to market with more concrete plan when finalized.

quotes.text: Vinay Lohariwala: "Both the engine can help the company to grow or maintain this 20% plus CAGR in the future."

points.label: Maintenance capex
points.text: FY27 and FY28 maintenance capex expected at ₹20 crore to ₹25 crore.

points.label: Growth capex
points.text: FY27 and FY28 growth capex expected at ₹20 crore to ₹30 crore.

points.label: R&D spend
points.text: Expected to remain in 0.7% to 1% of total revenue range.

points.label: Cash conversion cycle
points.text: Expected to be maintained at 90 days plus/minus 10 days at group level.

points.label: Semaglutide development
points.text: Status is "as is" from last con-call; development and plant team working on batches, closely watching.

items.title: Jammu facility ramp-up
items.text: Kathua's four-block greenfield plant (₹480+ cr capex) exited FY26 at a ₹90 cr quarterly run rate, hit ₹107 cr in Q1 FY27, and turned EBITDA-positive. Management targets ₹1,000 cr+ revenue from this facility in 2-3 years against ~25-30% utilization today - roughly 3x current total revenue if achieved.

items.title: Baddi general block expansion
items.text: Land acquired August 2025 for a new oral tablet/capsule and liquid facility, with capex estimated at ₹150-170 cr across FY27-FY28. At optimum level this block alone could add ₹450-500 cr revenue, relieving the capacity constraints currently capping the general portfolio.

items.title: Branded generics scale-up
items.text: Q1 FY27 branded generics revenue grew 39% YoY to ₹142.2 cr, following FY26's 51% jump to ₹497 cr. The business runs at ~70% domestic trade generics with 2,50,000+ touchpoints, and management is pushing into new geographies and products - the fastest-growing segment at roughly double the CDMO growth rate.

items.title: CDMO wallet-share expansion
items.text: CDMO revenue grew 32% YoY in Q1 FY27 to ₹328.7 cr, driven by new customers and higher wallet share from existing ones. With 350+ clients across 60+ countries and ~80% of revenue from partners served over 5 years, the model compounds through repeat orders and new contract wins without needing new capacity.

items.title: Sharon Bio-Medicine integration
items.text: Sharon (acquired June 2023) contributed ~₹240 cr revenue in FY26 with margins above company average, and is expected to grow in early teens organically. Its Dehradun and Taloja plants run at 60-70% utilization with room to 70-80%, and it opens regulated markets (Canada, UK, Europe, Australia) that the parent couldn't reach alone.

items.title: Regulatory approvals opening regulated markets
items.text: UK-MHRA approved the Baddi cephalosporin plant and PIC/S (SMDC Ukraine) certified the Kathua, Jammu facility in FY26. These certifications unlock sales into UK, Canada, and other regulated markets - exports already rose from 25.9% of revenue in FY25 to 31.3% in FY26.

items.title: Jammu GST incentive
items.text: The facility qualifies for GST-linked incentives totaling 300% of eligible plant and machinery investment over 10 years, plus 6% annual interest subvention on term loans. The GST rate cut on formulations (12% to 5%) means the full ~₹75-80 cr incentive now requires ~₹1,400 cr annual sales - which aligns with the facility's peak revenue potential.

items.title: Semaglutide and GLP-1 development
items.text: R&D work on semaglutide is underway with positive initial results, targeting a "wave 2" launch after the 2026 patent expiry of GLP-1 drugs. This is a high-value CDMO opportunity that could add a new revenue leg if the company captures even a small share of the generic wave.
